_metadata.data_source: Institute of Medicine (IOM) Dietary Reference Intakes, National Academies 2019 Sodium/Potassium Update, FDA, USDA, Clinical Research

vitamin_a.message: Too much preformed vitamin A over time can harm the liver. During pregnancy, it can cause birth defects.

vitamin_c.message: High intakes can cause diarrhea, nausea, and stomach cramps.

vitamin_d.message: Too much over time can raise blood calcium and increase the risk of kidney problems.

vitamin_e.message: High supplemental doses can increase the risk of bleeding.

niacin.message: Too much supplemental niacin can cause flushing, nausea, or liver problems; effects depend on the form.

vitamin_b6.message: Long-term excessive intake can cause nerve damage, numbness, or loss of coordination.

folate.message: Too much folic acid can hide a vitamin B12 deficiency and delay treatment.

choline.message: Too much can cause nausea, heavy sweating, low blood pressure, or a fishy body odor.

calcium.message: Excessive intake can cause constipation or nausea and may increase the risk of kidney stones.

magnesium.message: Too much supplemental magnesium can cause diarrhea, nausea, and stomach cramps.

iron.message: High supplemental doses can cause nausea, constipation, stomach pain, vomiting, or diarrhea.

zinc.message: Long-term excessive zinc can reduce copper absorption and lead to copper deficiency.

copper.message: Too much copper over time can cause stomach symptoms and damage the liver.

selenium.message: Too much over time can cause hair loss, brittle nails, nausea, and nervous-system symptoms.

iodine.message: Too much can disrupt thyroid function, especially in people with thyroid conditions.

manganese.message: Long-term excessive intake may affect the nervous system and movement.

molybdenum.message: Very high intake can cause joint pain and gout-like symptoms.

phosphorus.message: Very high intake can disrupt calcium balance; extreme doses can harm the kidneys.

chloride.message: Too much chloride, usually from salt, can raise blood pressure in some people.

fluoride.message: Too much over time can stain developing teeth and, at very high intakes, weaken bones.

boron.message: Too much can cause nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, rash, or headache.

vanadium.message: Excessive vanadium intake can harm the kidneys. The adult upper limit is 1.8 mg per day.

nickel.message: High soluble-nickel intake can cause harm. Nickel allergy or kidney problems may increase risk below the general limit.
